document_title: One Race Late. The limit and the money it missed.
post_copy:
105 top Alaska donors match what six Bay Area donors gave governor candidate Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins.

Six people who list Anthropic as their employer gave $372,000 between February 3rd and May 7th. The company gave nothing.
The median Alaska gift in that record is $50.
All of it was lawful. Alaska has had no individual contribution limit since a federal appeals court ruling in 2021.
The money went to the candidate proposing a data center moratorium.
On August 18th Alaskans voted 117,962 to 45,418 to restore limits. Alaska Public Media reported the measure would take effect after the November general election.

One sheet holds every gift in the 2026 record, photographed nine times, down to the inside of a single deposit.

Should a rule that passed with 72 percent wait for one more race?

#AlaskaGovernor #CampaignFinance #AIPolicy

first_comment:
A disclosure. This deck was produced by an automated studio running on Claude, a model made by Anthropic, and it reports on donations by six people who list Anthropic as their employer. The company gave nothing and no company statement about the donations is reported. Every figure here is arithmetic over the State of Alaska's own disclosure rows, recomputed twice by separate code, and an adversarial fact-check dropped twelve claims before publication.

Sources for today's deck.

Alaska Public Offices Commission, Campaign Disclosure Income, report year 2026, status Complete Not Amended, pulled September 5th, 2026. 4,604 transactions, 4,588 of them positive, $2,379,290.20 net.
https://aws.state.ak.us/ApocReports/CampaignDisclosure/CDIncome.aspx

Alaska Division of Elections, petition status for initiative 23RCF2, An Act restoring campaign contribution limits. YES 117,962, NO 45,418, approved by voters.
https://www.elections.alaska.gov/petitions-and-ballot-measures/petition-status/?initiative_id=23RCF2

Alaska Division of Elections, 23RCF2 bill text. New AS 15.13.070(b)(1) sets $2,000 each election cycle, and (g)(1) sets $4,000 for a joint governor and lieutenant governor candidacy.
https://www.elections.alaska.gov/petitions-and-ballot-measures/petition-status/petition_id/23rcf2

Alaska Division of Elections, 2026 primary results, marked Official and last updated August 31st, 2026.
https://www.elections.alaska.gov/election-results/e/?id=26prim

Alaska Division of Elections, certified candidates for the November 3rd, 2026 general election.
https://www.elections.alaska.gov/candidates/?election=26genr

Eric Stone, Alaska Public Media, August 18th, 2026, on the measure's limits and when it takes effect.
https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/elections/2026-08-18/campaign-finance-ballot-measure-passing-by-wide-margin

Emily Shugerman, The San Francisco Standard, August 31st, 2026, first reporting on the donations.
https://sfstandard.com/2026/08/31/anthropic-employees-alaska-governor-race-kreiss-tomkins/

Every figure about the money is arithmetic over the state's own disclosure rows and was recomputed twice by separate code. Every gift reported here was lawful when it was made.

editor_notes_for_email:
READ THE DISCLOSURE NOTE BEFORE POSTING. This routine runs on a Claude model built by Anthropic, and the deck reports on donations by six people who list Anthropic as their employer. The disclosure is the FIRST PARAGRAPH of the first comment above. If that comment does not go up with the post, do not post the deck.

Three things to check with your own eyes. First, plate 08 carries the only quote in the deck and its attribution was corrected this run: he said it to the Northern Journal, the San Francisco Standard reprinted it, and the request he did not answer was the Standard's. The earlier wording implied he ducked the outlet he had just spoken to. Second, no plate names a date for the measure taking effect, because no source gives one, and plate 09 says only that it follows the November general election. Third, gold on these nine plates means the $4,000 limit and nothing else; if you see gold on a donor, a dollar figure or a name, that is a defect and the deck should not go up until it is fixed.

The deck went through THREE full build rounds. The first pixel-critic pass scored it 4.8 against a threshold of 8.3 and the run rebuilt rather than shipping a post-mortem; the second averaged 6.2. Four BUILD RECONCILIATION tables in the storyboard record every change and why, including two factual corrections, two places where the plan of record itself was wrong, and one place where a critic's prescribed fix was wrong and the opposite was done.

A review of the shipped commit then caught five more, all corrected before the merge, and the most important is worth knowing about: the disclosure was named in these notes as being in the first comment and was NOT in it. It is now. The other four narrowed claims that were too wide. Plate 01's rings are the 105 largest Alaska GIFTS ($354,294.88); C14's 105 counts DONORS ($372,960.85), and the plate now prints both and says the sheet draws gifts while the headline counts donors. If a reader challenges the cover's arithmetic, that distinction is the answer.

Scored 8.77. The score was taken before those five corrections and the deck was not re-scored a third time; score_report.json records exactly what changed afterwards and why.
aftercare: This deck reports on political donations by six named private individuals. If a comment names any of them abusively, hide the comment rather than replying to it. The deck's own position is that every gift was lawful and that no exchange is evidenced, and that position has to hold in the replies too.

If anyone reads the deck as saying Anthropic gave money, correct it in one line and quote the plate: the company gave nothing, six people did, and the employer field is a string those six typed on a disclosure form.
The conflict of interest is real and is disclosed in the first comment. If a reader raises it, agree with them and point at the disclosure rather than defending the deck.

Two numbers will be challenged. 4,588 is positive contributions and 4,604 is transactions including refunds, and plate 01 prints both. 86 is donors who gave more than $4,000 in total while 93 is the count of maximum contributions the six gifts equal, and they are different quantities that happen to sit near each other.

The measure's start date is the one thing not to improvise on. No published source gives a date, only that it takes effect after the November general election, and the deck says exactly that and no more.

If the Northern Journal or the San Francisco Standard responds, do not argue attribution in public. Plate 08 says he spoke to the Northern Journal and did not answer the Standard's own request, which is what the two sources support.

If anyone measures the cover, the rings are the 105 largest Alaska gifts and they sum to $354,294.88. The claim that 105 match the six is about donors grouped by name, city and state, who sum to $372,960.85. The plate prints both and says the sheet draws gifts. That is the honest answer and it is stronger than deflecting.
